sentences.text: This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail, pending the trial.
The applicant is in custody since 20.07.2021 in connection with Crime No.23/2021, registered at P.S.-Panwar, District- Rewa (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 294 and 506-B of IPC.
As per the prosecution story, applicant had assigned work of installation of Jio poles to one Sandeep Kumar Mishra.
Some amount of money was paid to the complainant by the applicant in cash towards the payment of work done.

sentences.text: It is alleged that for remaining amount cheques amounting Rs. 24 lacs were given to Sandeep Kumar Mishra.
When he presented the cheques in the Bank, same was refused as dishonored.
On the basis of complaint made by the complainant, FIR for commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that he is already facing trial for the cases of cheque bounce.
It is contended that in a case where cheque has stood bounce, an offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is made out.
No offence under Section 420 of IPC is made out.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant cannot be prosecuted in two different cases for the same offence.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail and has submitted that cases are registered against the applicant at different police stations for commission of same type of offences.
Therefore, it is prayed that he be not released on bail.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Offence is triable by the JMFC.
Applicant is in jail for more than one year and six months.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.

Therefore,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail is allowed.

It is directed that applicant-Kaustubh Rishi be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vkv /-
